## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

This one-fascicle short sūtra (T510) by [竺曇無蘭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%98%AD) Zhú Tánwúlán narrates an unusual *vyākaraṇa* story: a flower-picker disobeys his royal employer in order to offer flowers to the Buddha and consequently receives the prediction of attaining buddhahood with the future title *Miàohuā* 妙花 ("Wonderful Flower"). The text presents the Mahāyāna principle that direct devotion to the Buddha overrides feudal-political duty.

**Abstract**

A short Mahāyāna devotional narrative on the supremacy of Buddha-veneration over secular duty. Translation dated to Tánwúlán's Eastern Jìn period (381–395 CE).
